newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: No changes in Kazakh gas deal, official says.
newsitem.headline: No changes in Kazakh gas deal, official says.

text.p: There have been no changes in the proposed distribution of shares in a project to develop Kazakhstan's giant Karachaganak gas field, a senior Kazakh gas industry official said.
Vyacheslav Nupov, vice president of the state Kazakhgaz company, told Reuters he was unaware of any plans by British Gas to cut its 42.5 percent stake.
"No official decision has been made on this. Everything remains as it was before," he said.

FSU Energy, a weekly newsletter published by Petroleum Argus, reported last week that British Gas wanted to cut its stake and scale back overseas operations because of intense competitive pressure in Britain's domestic market.
Nupov could not say if there would be changes in the Karachaganak deal. "The official contract has not yet been signed," he said.
British Gas representatives in Almaty were not available for comment.
Other partners in the proposed Karachaganak consortium are Italy's Agip Spa (42.5 percent) and Russia's Gazprom (15 percent).
However, Nupov said back in July that Russia's biggest oil producer LUKoil would acquire Gazprom's 15 percent stake.
Karachaganak, one of Kazakhstan's largest hydrocarbon deposits, is in the northwest of the former Soviet republic.
Recoverable reserves are estimated at 1.33 trillion cubic metres of natural gas, 644 million tonnes of gas condensate and 189 million tonnes of crude oil.
British Gas and Agip signed a preliminary agreement in March 1995 on the $10 billion, 40-year project.
The project foresees upgrading existing facilities and stopping a decline in the field's output.
